newsitem.title: USA: ShopKo gains after merger deal scotched.
newsitem.headline: ShopKo gains after merger deal scotched.

text.p: Shares of ShopKo Stores Inc rose in early trading on Wednesday on expectations that its major shareholder would be able to find a new deal to replace the $1 billion merger with Phar-Mor Inc.
Earlier, the companies said their $1 billion merger was called off due to "continuing uncertainties".
ShopKo shares rose 7/8 to 16-1/8. The early gain may have been triggered by a statement made by ShopKo president and chief executive, Dale Kramer, according to one arbitrageur.

Kramer said: "We are confident that those goals -- expanding both the scale and scope of our business and providing an exit strategy for Supervalu in a way that benefits remaining shareholders -- can be achieved".

The statement, made in the press release announcing the dissolution of the merger, is leading investors to bet that ShopKo and Supervalu are pursuing a mutually beneficial exit plan which could boost the shareholder value of ShopKo.
Supervalu Inc owns about 46 percent of ShopKo. It said it backed the decision to call off the merger and is still committed to exiting its investment in ShopKo.
Supervalu shares slipped 1/4 to 29-1/2. The company had said it expected an unspecified gain of as part of the merger.
Phar-Mor shares also rose, adding 1/2 to 5-1/2.
But arbitrageurs said they did not expect volatile stock activity in the wake of the announcement, because many had stayed on the sidelines of the marriage, which they said had a "tentative" quality.

"This deal had a mechanical arb problems -- it was hard to borrow Phar-Mor stock, the terms were very complicated -- but also it was not a very clearly defined agreement. There were too many contingencies, too many outs," said one arb who declined to be identified.

Under terms of the now defunct deal, drug retailer Phar-Mor would have merged with retailer ShopKo, creating a new company to be called Cabot Noble Inc. Cabot would have had combined annual sales of about $3.2 billion and 232 stores in 29 states.
